newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Keppel FELS propects weak - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Keppel FELS propects weak - analysts.

text.p: Prospects for Keppel Corp's off-shore rigbuilding and repair unit, Keppel FELS Ltd (FELS), is seen as poor with the company warning of lower profit in 1997, analysts said on Monday.
They said FELS' share price, which has been under pressure in recent weeks, could see a decline of another 10 percent after it warned of "substantially lower" 1997 results.
FELS ended unchanged at S$5.75 on Monday with 172,000 shares traded.
In a statement accompanying the results for the financial year ended December 31 1996, FELS said 1997 results would be substantially lower "as there are no major completions this year".

"Share prices are expected to drop by about 10 percent. Before the results, Singapore $5.75 was seen as a good base price but after the results, that's unlikely," said an analyst with a local brokerage house.
It reported an 18.1 percent growth in net profit in 1996 to S$54.36 million while turnover grew 30.7 percent to S$854.99 million.

FELS said the higher 1996 turnover was due to the completed constructions of two floating production storage and offloading vessels (FPSOs) for Smedvig and Statoil, a topside production facility for the Wandoo Alliance and the conversion and sale of a vessel to Transocean.
Several completed repair jobs, including those involving AMFELS, its U.S. subsidiary, also contributed to the higher turnover.
Analysts told Reuters the lower contributions from the two completed FPSOs were not surprising but fuelled concerns over the company's prospects.

"They have been forthcoming in their projections for a tough year ahead. The margins they have achieved are a concern. Are the jobs they have on hand going to be profitable?" said an analyst at a European house.

"FELS' comment that there are no major completions this year implies some jobs have been delayed to 1998. This would be fine because 1998 would show some growth but to begin with 1998 looks empty," the analyst with the local brokerage house said.
"Our greatest worry is FELS have not won any major jobs. They have actually lost some contracts to the Japanese and the Koreans," she added.
